answer:
Here is what I would bring up, most important first. The newest record I have is from July 14, 2026, so anything after that will not show here.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide may still be in use. Kestrel Harbor Hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026 because your sodium had dropped to 123. But the pharmacy still lists it as active, with a fill on April 2, 2026 and two refills left. Your May eye-clinic list shows it as taken, and your Fernhill list from June still shows it as active. Fernhill's June note says to continue current medications. Your June sodium was still a little low at 134. Please confirm with the pharmacy and Dr. Marsh whether you are taking it, and have it removed from every list if it has been stopped.

2. The thyroid recheck is overdue. Your TSH was 7.9 (high) on March 3, with a normal free T4. The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated 6 to 8 weeks after discharge, which is late April. I do not see a repeat in any record. Your sodium has not been checked since June 15.

3. The lung spot needs its follow-up scan. The CT at the Saltmarsh emergency department on October 18, 2025, done for the kidney stone, also found a 7 mm solid spot in the right lower lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months, so that window closed around October 18, 2026. Nothing after that visit mentions the spot or a scan.

4. Cholesterol and a statin. In September 2025 your LDL was 142, total cholesterol 221, HDL 48 (low), and triglycerides 155. You were diagnosed with type 2 diabetes that month, and guidelines usually recommend a statin for people with diabetes your age. No statin is on any of your lists, and there has been no cholesterol test since September 2025.

5. Vaccines. The second Shingrix dose is not recorded. It was due 2 to 6 months after the first on November 8, 2025. No flu shot for this season is recorded, and I see no Tdap or COVID vaccine anywhere. Prevnar 20 from the same visit is complete. Fernhill's vaccine list also leaves out the November 2025 shots.

6. Diabetes checks. Your A1c was 6.6% on June 15, so the next one is due about now. No urine kidney test (albumin-to-creatinine ratio) and no foot exam appear in any record. Your eye exam on May 14, 2026 found no diabetic eye damage, and the next is due in May 2027. Ask whether you went to the diabetes education visit suggested in September 2025. Mammogram and cervical screening also do not appear in these records, though they may have been done elsewhere. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, so the next is due around 2029.

7. The kidney stone follow-up. The emergency department asked you to see your primary doctor within a week, and urology if the stone had not passed in two weeks. Nothing in your records shows either visit or a repeat urine test. Ask whether a repeat urine test is needed to confirm the blood in your urine has cleared.

8. Fernhill's record is missing recent events. It does not mention the October kidney stone visit, the lung spot, or the March hospital stay for low sodium, including the fall at home without injury. Its problem list has no low sodium entry. Please ask Fernhill to add these and to get the hospital and emergency summaries.

9. Lisinopril cough. Fernhill lists lisinopril as an intolerance (dry cough, 2025), but the hospital and pharmacy allergy lists show only aspirin. Ask for it to be added to every list so an ACE inhibitor is not given to you again by mistake.

10. Amlodipine start date. It was prescribed April 1, 2025, but this pharmacy's first fill was September 27, 2025. You may have filled it somewhere else. If not, you may have gone without it for several months, so it is worth checking.

I am not your doctor, so please confirm these points with Dr. Marsh.

knowledge.says: For diabetes, guidelines suggest an A1c every 3 to 6 months, a yearly urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and kidney function test, a yearly foot exam, and a yearly lipid panel. Eye exams are usually yearly, or every 1 to 2 years once normal. For screening, mammograms are usually every 2 years from age 40 to 74, and cervical screening is recommended from 21 to 65.
knowledge.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes; US Preventive Services Task Force screening recommendations
